All right, welcome to how to diagram inclusion and inclusion is really just either or It has a fancy name and it sounds nice with exclusion, but it really it doesn't have a family.
0:11
It's just either or Which I I think it's a fight up I call it inclusion just because I really wanted to highlight The action of what you have to do when you see an either or in the logical reason
0:23
You have to include at least one half of the pair that's modified by the either or and so the basic way that we go about diagramming an either or statement an inclusion statement is that we say if I don't have one half of this pair then I must have the other half
0:41
And so mechanically the way that works is I take one half of the statement I put in sufficient condition and I negate it
0:48
and then it leads Through my necessary arrow into a necessary condition. That's just the other half of the pair unchanged not negated
0:56
And so let's see how it works with an example Okay, so either the cats will sleep or they will riot
1:03
Okay, so we see our either or here right that tells us we're dealing with inclusion and we also see that we have two halves of a pair right
1:13
or two or two items that are being modified by either or or the cats will sleep or The cats will riot
1:20
and so we want to be able to make a conditional statement that will allow for the fact that if I don't Have one of these I must have the other at least one of them is required or
1:29
I could have both and so or on the Elisabeth you might remember me saying in other videos is Inclusive meaning when I see that or it's not saying I can only have one of these and I can't have both
1:40
and so I Want and however I draw however I represent my either or I want to allow for that possibility as well that you know I could have both of these
1:49
I don't want to necessarily preclude having both in the way that I diagram it and so let's see What we come up with all right
1:54
so we can take either half of the sentence I'm gonna start with this half of the sentence this first one here, and I'm gonna say okay if I don't have that If the cats are not sleeping then and now I'm gonna take my other half of the sentence the one right here And I will say okay those cats will riot
2:13
Look at that Okay, and so just to answer a couple of questions about why I did this exactly the way that I did you might be asking yourself Hey, Ellen,
2:21
why is that C here in the CR? There's no C on that second half of the sentence, and that's because I'm translating referentially friends They will riot is talking about the cats
2:31
and so to me It's a little bit CLIRer for me to be able to read this statement say okay if the cats are not sleeping Then the cats are writing of course
2:39
you could just also have written this as like not sleep arrow riot Like that's also entirely possible like I'm not against you if you did that But I think it's a little bit CLIR to just have that CR there.
2:50
That's why I did it It's just referential Translation trying to make things easier for myself now the other thing you might have asked is like hey Do I have to do it so that I have this first half of the sentence as the one that is going here in our Sufficient condition
3:05
could I have done it where I chose the second half of the sentence to go in the sufficient condition Why yes friends you could have it does not actually matter which side of the statement you pick it So I'll demo it right now just to show you what it would look like if I had chosen The second half of the sentence as my sufficient condition and then negated that
3:21
so they will riot Let me do that here in our sufficient as okay if the cats do not riot Then I must have my other half of the pair
3:31
I must have the cat sleeping and so you may notice one thing here, huh? These two statements are contra positives of one another right
3:39
they actually have equivalent meaning That's why it doesn't matter whether I pick the first half of the sentence to put in the sufficient and negate or the second half Of the sentence to put in the sufficient negate doesn't matter either way because no matter what I pick I get an equivalent statement
3:52
And it's just a matter of usability. I personally tend to use the first half of the sentence this guy More in the sufficient condition than I pick the second half, but honestly that's just you know It's a personal preference typically it leads to a more easy to parse grammatical way of
4:09
thinking about it But absolutely not a requirement and so Let's go to our next one and just see how this works when we have one of them being negated in the actual statement itself
4:18
So alright either if the tree will grow or it will not grant wishes Wish granting tree. Okay, so we have our either or right here, and we've got our two halves of our pair Right.
4:32
All right, and so let's just start by putting the first half of the sentence in our negated sufficient condition
4:39
So we say okay if this tree does not grow then and then I have my second half of the statement And I'm gonna put that in my necessary condition unchanged then it will not Grant wishes.
4:50
Okay. Now I've got a double negated statement. That's kind of gnarly, right? I don't really like double negated statements But again, there's just a personal preference.
4:56
They're kind of hard to read kind of hard to translate personally if I Were to be diagramming any sort of conditional in any LR section and I got something that looked like this I would very quickly just take the contra positive and then cross out the original
5:10
basically I would do this right here I would say okay. Well the contra positive of this is if grant wishes then tree grow.
5:17
All right, so forget about you friend Goodbye. Goodbye, and then I would only work with this statement and Like I said, that's simply a usability perspective of it's a lot easier typically to work with positive Statements rather than negated statements just because the brain it kind of takes an extra
5:35
step sometimes with negations It can get more easily confused Especially when double negations are involved and so it can be really nice to actually just contra positive that to the positive side of the stage
5:45
But I hope this helped in terms of filling out your understanding of inclusion see what it's really not that bad
5:50
It's just one little thing to remember and when it does come up You're gonna be super super grateful that you did remember because it clarifies a lot of stuff takes some of the harder questions out There it makes them a lot more doable And so I hope that this helped
6:01
